findings.title: Giving as the next stage of sustained care
findings.claim: The promised giving can be perceived as the next stage of a Lordly care process: the transfer continues an administered course of nurture and reaches the addressee as satisfaction.
findings.mechanism: The focus giving, Lord-title, and satisfaction carriers meet the supplied direct giving, ordered-care, uncut-gift, and future-satisfaction contacts, while 93:6-8 supplies a prior sequence of shelter, guidance, and sufficiency. Their contact changes the future transfer from an isolated event into another phase of care already shown in operation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the promise as a further episode in a continuing care relation rather than as an unnamed object arriving without a history.
findings.containment: The primary reading remains 'Rabbin sana mutlaka verecek, sen de hoşnut olacaksın.' The staged-care relation adds a contextual contour; it does not name the withheld object, replace giving with nurture, or select one material form of the promise.

epistemic.reason: Trusted focus-anchored publication evidence and direct connection records support the relation, while the represented reader-walk supports are legacy_unbound and the connection targets do not supply full target morphology.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: verme, karşılıklı elden geçirme ve verilen şey

branch_activations.carrier: The focus verb carries directed giving and transfer to the explicit addressee.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 78:36 supplies a measured gift from the Lord, and the supplied 93:6-8 sequence gives prior episodes of received care.
branch_activations.activation: The giving carrier meets measured provision and the prior care sequence, so the future transfer becomes a further administered stage rather than a detached event.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The promised gift is felt as another concrete transfer within a continuing course of care.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus Form IV giving direction remains primary; no object or material form of the gift is invented.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Süreç, gözetilen şeyi eksik durumdan tamamlanmış duruma doğru geliştirir.
branch_activations.carrier: The definite Lord-title carries the relation of sustaining, ordering, and bringing the cared-for person toward completion.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 20:50 joins giving each thing with guidance, 65:2 joins a way out with provision, and 93:6-8 supplies the prior corrective sequence.
branch_activations.activation: The Lord-title meets ordered provision and the prior shelter-guidance-sufficiency sequence, making the future giving legible as the next step in developmental care.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The promise extends an already active process of being brought from need toward completion.
branch_activations.boundary: The completion pressure colors the Lord-title here; it does not turn the ayah into a full biography or a deterministic timeline.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Hoşnutluk, öfke ve hoşnutsuzluğun karşıtı olan olumlu kabul durumudur.
branch_activations.carrier: The future second-person satisfaction carrier names the recipient-side resolution of the promise.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 92:21 directly joins future expectation to satisfaction, while 11:108 describes an enduring gift; the 93:6-8 sequence supplies the preceding care history.
branch_activations.activation: The satisfaction carrier meets future and enduring-gift contacts, so completion is measured at the recipient's settled state as well as at the act of transfer.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The gift's further stage is recognized by the addressee's arriving at acceptance and contentment.
branch_activations.boundary: The addressee's satisfaction remains the plain result; endurance and developmental sequence are contextual contours, not a replacement gloss.

findings.title: Satisfaction as reciprocal approval
findings.claim: The satisfaction named at the end of the ayah can also be perceived as a reciprocal approval relation in which the giver and recipient arrive at an accepted outcome together.
findings.mechanism: The focus satisfaction carrier meets the supplied mutual divine-human approval contacts at 98:8 and 5:119. The external relation makes the recipient's contentment open toward an approval shared across the giver-recipient relation rather than remaining only an interior mood.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear 'hoşnut olacaksın' as an outcome that settles a relation, not only as comfort privately felt by the addressee.
findings.containment: The ayah still grammatically promises that the addressee will be satisfied. Reciprocal approval is a contextual extension of that result; it does not change the subject of the satisfaction verb or claim that the ayah explicitly states mutual consent.

epistemic.reason: The trusted support and exact focus carrier are present, but the support is weakly graded and the connection targets are supplied without full target morphology.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Hoşnutluk ve kabul iki taraf arasında karşılıklı olarak kurulur.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus satisfaction verb carries the addressee's resulting acceptance and contentment.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 98:8 and 5:119 supply explicit mutual divine-human approval relations.
branch_activations.activation: The recipient-side satisfaction carrier meets wider mutual-approval relations, so contentment acquires a relational settlement dimension.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The promised satisfaction can be felt as approval that settles the relation between giver and recipient.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus remains a second-person result; mutuality is a contextual resonance, not an invented reciprocal subject in the grammar.

findings.title: Receiving opens capacity for service
findings.claim: The giving addressed to the addressee can also be perceived as opening the capacity to attend to another person's needs, so received provision becomes usable service.
findings.mechanism: The focus giving carrier meets 24:33's supplied image of giving others from wealth already received. That independent outward-giving relation changes the gift from a closed possession into a capacity that can be spent in attending to others.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices an onward direction in the promised gift: what reaches the addressee can become attention and help for someone else.
findings.containment: The primary promise of giving to the addressee remains intact. Service is a later capacity opened by the gift, not the unnamed object of the verb and not an explicit command in 93:5.

epistemic.reason: The trusted focus-anchored support, exact giving carrier, and direct supplied giving-to-others connection establish a bounded outward-service relation; target morphology remains outside the claim.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir başkasının işini görme ve bakımını üstlenme eylemidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus Form IV verb carries giving directed to the explicit second-person recipient.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 24:33 supplies the wider relation of giving others from wealth already received.
branch_activations.activation: The directed-giving carrier meets the outward-service image, so reception becomes a source of attentive capacity for another person.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The promised gift can equip the addressee to become an attentive giver.
branch_activations.boundary: The service branch is a contextual consequence of receiving; the focus verb still directly names the Lord's giving to the addressee.

findings.title: A reversible ask-and-give circuit
findings.claim: The focus giving form can be opened into a reversible social circuit: one position receives a transfer while another voices need, and the same field of giving accommodates both positions.
findings.mechanism: The focus giving carrier lands the transfer facet and the asking facet, while 34:39 supplies circulation and replacement, 28:24 supplies articulated need before the Lord, and 14:34 supplies response to requests. These contacts make the giver-recipient relation a circuit in which today's recipient can later stand in the position of the requester.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the unnamed gift as entering a living economy of receiving and asking rather than ending at private possession.
findings.containment: The focus Form IV construction still selects directed giving to the addressee. The asking branch is a wider root-family resonance; it does not make the focus subject an asker or replace the promised transfer with a request.

epistemic.reason: Both nominated focus branches have exact carriers, the trusted support explicitly joins giving and asking, and the request/circulation connections provide independent wider contacts.

findings.title: The manner of giving bends toward need
findings.claim: The promised giving can also be sensed as a yielding movement toward need: the giver's approach is colored by pliancy, while the later prohibitions make non-coercive care a relevant form of receiving and passing on what was received.
findings.mechanism: The focus giving carrier meets the B006 pliancy facet, the 93:9-10 prohibitions against overpowering and rebuking, and 26:22's boundary between claimed favor and domination. The contact changes the manner of the promise from transfer alone to transfer whose approach bends toward the vulnerable.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive gentleness as part of how the promised care arrives, and can see why received care would matter for conduct toward vulnerable people.
findings.containment: The primary reading remains the Lord's future giving to the addressee. The focus verb does not lexically mean bending, and the ethical transfer from receiving to conduct is a qualified contextual inference.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication is weakly graded and the reader-walk is legacy_unbound, but both supply the focus branch and the packet supplies the anti-domination context and a wider boundary contact.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Yayın sert ve direngen olmayıp kolayca bükülmesini ve gerilmesini anlatır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus giving verb carries the supplied pliancy pressure as a possible manner of approaching the recipient.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 93:9-10 supply the later anti-domination and anti-rebuke sequence, while 26:22 marks domination as a boundary on claimed favor.
branch_activations.activation: The pliancy carrier meets the independent anti-domination contacts, so giving can be perceived as bending toward need rather than imposing force.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The promise includes a qualified image of care arriving without coercive pressure.
branch_activations.boundary: Pliancy is a contextual manner-of-giving resonance; it does not replace the ordinary directed-giving sense or assert a necessary causal law.

findings.title: Provision as a boundary against anxious overreach
findings.claim: Because the focus makes the Lord the giver and the addressee the satisfied recipient, its overreach and contest images can function as a boundary: fulfilled provision is perceived as removing pressure to seize beyond one's right or win by force.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries the overreach, contest, and satisfaction branches together. The supplied anti-domination sequence at 93:9-10 and the wider contrast contacts at 26:22, 54:29, and 92:16 give those latent images an independent boundary, changing the promise into a contrast between received provision and anxious taking.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the promise as relieving the need to grasp, overreach, or establish worth by defeating another person, while the literal gift-and-satisfaction movement remains visible.
findings.containment: The primary promise stays intact. The supplied publication itself grades this contrast as reject, so the relation is retained only as a qualified boundary inference; the ayah does not explicitly state that receiving cancels every form of striving or contest.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication marks the comparison reject, while the legacy walk supplies the nominated overpowering context and the packet supplies focus carriers plus independent contrast contacts. The resulting boundary is therefore explicit but inferential.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Karşılıklı bir girişim veya çekişme içinde öteki tarafa o konuda üstün gelinir.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 93:9-10 prohibit oppressive handling, and 92:16 supplies a rejection-and-turning-away contrast that delimits the generous path.
branch_activations.activation: The contest image meets anti-domination and turning-away boundaries, so satisfaction can be felt as an outcome not purchased by defeating the other.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The promise offers a recipient-side settlement alongside the live image of competitive victory.
branch_activations.boundary: The contest facet is not asserted as the literal meaning of the satisfaction verb and does not erase other live satisfaction readings.

branch_activations.boundary: The focus Form IV occurrence remains directed giving; no literal unlawful-taking event is assigned to 93:5.

branch_activations.activation: The victory image meets those independent boundaries, so the future gift can be perceived as an outcome that does not depend on winning a contest.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Satisfaction remains the promised result while anxious victory is held at the edge of the reading.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a qualified countervailing image, not a claim that the focus verb names contest or that striving is categorically excluded.

branch_activations.boundary: The branch is a nominated contextual image with no independent lexicon facet in the packet; no unstated gloss or target morphology is added.

findings.title: Satisfaction settles an answering relation

findings.mechanism: The focus mutual-approval carrier meets the supplied later questioner, favor, and affirmation sequence. The 5:119 approval contact and 14:34 request-response contact independently support a relation in which receiving and answering are connected without turning the focus promise into a command to serve.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel satisfaction as a stable base for responsive relationship, not as a private endpoint that ends movement.
findings.containment: The focus still promises the addressee's satisfaction. The answering-yes image is a nominated contextual resonance from the supplied 93:11 reference, and no full lexical analysis is invented for it.

epistemic.reason: The reader walk supplies exact pericope references and focus branch identity, but explicitly presents the reciprocity arrow as an inference and the affirmation branch as a nominated source image.

branch_activations.activation: The mutual-satisfaction carrier meets later asking and affirmation, so contentment becomes a relational settlement that remains open to response.

branch_activations.boundary: This is an attributed source image with no supplied lexicon facet statement; the focus is not recast as an affirmation verb.

findings.title: The promise opens into ethical conduct and telling
findings.claim: The promise can be perceived retrospectively as an ethical template: receiving the gift opens non-coercive conduct toward the orphan and asker, while satisfaction becomes a settled base from which favor can still be spoken.
findings.mechanism: The focus giving and satisfaction carriers return through the supplied 93:9-11 sequence. The later prohibitions export the manner of received care into conduct, and the final favor-and-speech unit prevents the recipient's satisfaction from becoming mute closure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the promised future as something that changes how the recipient handles vulnerable others and how the recipient speaks about what was received.
findings.containment: The primary promise remains recoverable as future giving followed by satisfaction. The ethical and narrative export is a retrospective pericope-level inference; it does not claim that 93:5 itself contains the later prohibitions or speech command.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective walk supplies the exact focus anchor and names the 93:9-11 before-and-after movement, but its ethical arrows are explicitly source-level inference.
